extracted.intended_audience: investigators and mentors preparing NIH Individual Career Development (K series) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and guidance for preparing and finding NIH Individual Career Development (K series) award applications, including purpose, typical award components, eligibility by career stage, mechanism mapping, where review criteria live, and related funding options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope note: purpose of K awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH career development awards (often referred to as the "K" series) provide support for mentored research career development experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career development (K) awards are intended for investigators at earlier phases of their research career to enhance skills development and provide time for research and training activities in the biomedical, behavioral, or clinical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical award components and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: These awards typically provide three to five years of salary, mentored research support, and protected time under the guidance of an experienced mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan proposals that allocate protected research/training time, include mentored research support, and address salary support for the proposed award duration (typically 3–5 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find official review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To find the criteria reviewers will use to evaluate your application, see Section V of your funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent Announcements include the minimum standard review criteria appropriate for their program. Applicants must consult the specific Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) — Section V — for the exact review criteria applicable to their application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / definition: Postdoctoral/Residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral refers to a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced training for those who have received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue their chosen career path. Residency refers to a graduate medical education program that provides physicians with hands-on experience and training in a specific medical specialty after they graduate from medical school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether your career stage fits K mechanisms intended for postdoctoral/residency applicants and select the appropriate activity code/mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / definition: Early Career
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage during which early career researchers are about to transition - or have recently moved - to fully independent positions as investigators, faculty members, clinician scientists, or scientific team leaders in industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants at this stage should consider K mechanisms aimed at facilitating transition to independence and protected time for establishing an independent research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / definition: Established Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage at which investigator leads research programs in an academic, industry, or government setting with independent (often peer-reviewed) research funding and have delivered significant research outputs due to their experience and scientific quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain K mechanisms (e.g., K05, K07, K18, K24, K25, K26) are applicable to midcareer or established investigators; match mechanism to your career stage/needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs by career stage / mechanism mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of K mechanisms appropriate to career stages (Postdoctoral/Residency, Early Career, Established Investigator). Examples include: Research Scientist Development Award - Research and Training (K01); Academic/Teacher Award (K07); Clinical Investigator Award (K08); Career Transition Award (K22); Mentored Patient-Oriented Research Career Development Award (K23); Mentored Quantitative Research Career Development Award (K25); International Research Career Development Award (K43); Emerging Leaders Career Development Award (K76); Career Transition Award (K99/R00); Senior Research Scientist Award (K05); Career Enhancement Award (K18); Midcareer Investigator Award in Patient-Oriented Research (K24); Midcareer Investigator Award in Biomedical and Behavioral Research (K26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mechanism mapping to identify which specific K activity code(s) align with your career stage and goals when searching FOAs and preparing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Transition Award (K99/R00) role
rubrics_metrics.description: Career Transition Award (Pathway to Independence Award) (K99)/(R00)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is specifically identified as intended to support transition to independent positions; applicants aiming to move to independence should evaluate eligibility and requirements of the K99/R00 pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplements as an option
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative supplement is a non-competing award that provides additional funding to a currently funded grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH participates in specific supplement programs such as Research Supplements to Promote Re-entry and Re-integration into Health-Related Research Careers and Research Continuity Supplements. Applicants with existing grants should consider applicable supplement opportunities as a funding route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternative funding mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Also Consider... — alternative/other NIH funding mechanisms suggested for early career investigators (e.g., Stephen I. Katz Early Stage Investigator Research Project Grant; Maximizing Investigators Research Award (MIRA) for Early Stage Investigators (R35); NIH Director's New Innovator Award (DP2); Administrative Supplements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early career applicants should compare K awards with other available mechanisms (R01-equivalents, R35, DP2) to determine the best fit for career goals and research needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and application resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for Individual Career Development Funding Opportunities — Use the Explore NIH Grant Opportunities tool to search Grants.gov. View Current Funding Opportunities. Ready to develop your application? Learn from a step-by-step guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are directed to NIH tools and step-by-step guides for finding FOAs and preparing applications; they should use these resources and consult institute/center-specific funding considerations and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/Center-specific funding considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Institute, Center, and Office (ICO) — Funding Considerations for Individual Career Development. View More. Funding Considerations for Individual Career Development — View More.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review ICO-specific guidance and funding considerations when preparing applications, as institutes may have program-specific expectations or contacts.
